newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX at higher levels in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX at higher levels in listless trade.

text.p: German shares continued their rebound in late afternoon trade on Tuesday, with sentiment underpinned by Wednesday's dramatic recovery on Wall Street but with sentiment on the market remaining nervous.
The IBIS DAX was up nearly two percent in the afternoon but dealers said that trade was generally listless.

"It's a bounce alright, but nobody knows whether to trust it or not. We weren't particularly surprised at the recovery in the U.S. -- it could only happen there. But the bottom line is that people are nervous, people are on holiday and nobody seems to want to get involved," a trader said.
The IBIS DAX stood at 4,156.72 points, up 76.17 points in afternoon trade. Earlier the DAX index ended bourse trade up 91.02 points at 4,169.62 points.
"Everyone is just following bonds, following the dollar and looking to the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting tonight," the trader said.
The dollar, which has lost a considerable amount of ground against the mark of late, looked stable at around 1.83 marks.
Bayer AG was up 1.31 marks at 71.60 marks after the chemicals and pharmaceuticals group said net profit for the first half of 1997 rose 13 percent to 1.7 billion marks.
Bayer also reported an 11 percent rise in sales to 27.4 billion marks.

Volkswagen AG was also higher in afternoon IBIS after reporting strong first-half results on Monday. Shares in the Wolfsburg-based carmaker percent rose by 74 marks at 1,357 marks in the afternoon after it said on Monday group net profit rose 73 percent in the first six months of the year.

VW chief executive Ferdinand Piech also said in a television interview on Monday that VW expected a good 700,000 orders in Europe for its new Golf model, to be unveiled on Tuesday in Bonn, in the first year of production.
German banks shares were notably higher after incurring heavy losses in the previous days.
Commerzbank AG, considered a prime takeover target in growing speculation about further industry mergers, was up 4.29 marks, around 6.70 percent, at 68.30 marks.
Deutsche Bank was up 2.90 marks at 114.25 marks, while Dresdner Bank AG was up 2.95 marks at 80.80 marks.
